miniProject.title: Tensor, sequence and context parallelism with owned layouts
miniProject.brief: Extend `trainlab` with tensor, sequence and context parallel mechanisms over the tiny transformer, each checked against a single-process oracle on CPU. Sharded layouts, collective records and timing models make degree choices testable instead of inherited.
steps: Build the paired column-to-row MLP in `parallel/` with explicit Gloo communication, and reconstruct outputs plus input and weight gradients against the `model/` oracle, keeping collective records. Anchor the linear path with the TensorTonic column-parallel problem and the ported Picotron linear tests.

Extend the layout to grouped-query attention and SwiGLU in `parallel/`, preserving query-to-value mapping and matching gate and up shards, checked against the `model/` oracle for outputs and gradients. Run the TorchFeather attention and SwiGLU examples, then cover the grouped-query ownership variation the examples omit.

Add vocabulary-parallel embedding and sharded cross-entropy in `parallel/` with per-token reductions, tied-weight accumulation and range checks against ordinary cross-entropy. Add sequence-sharded norms and residuals with per-rank gain-gradient sums, layout assertions and saved-versus-temporary accounting.

Express the layouts as `DTensor` placements on a named mesh in `comm/`, with group manifests, boundary assertions and forward and backward oracle comparisons. Keep a transition suite that reconstructs each layout and records the backend-aware collective behind every communicating move.

Build the ring-attention path in `parallel/` with streamed key-value visits, online softmax state and remote-gradient returns, removing the redundant rotation and rechecking outputs and gradients. Cover packed-document masks, rotary alignment and indexed dropout replay with negative cases plus uneven-shard, padding, invalid-target and ownership-mutation oracles.

Derive the per-rank ledger in `plan/` after working the JAX matmul-strategies question. Tabulate feasible degree candidates with a bandwidth-sensitive timing model and matched correctness and timing records for the sync and async paths, with GPU overlap traces only with two or more GPUs.
deliverables: The `parallel/` tensor, sequence and context mechanisms with oracles, manifests and collective records.
The `plan/` ledger, candidate table and timing model with synchronous and asynchronous records.
`tests/` replaying every oracle and negative case plus `reports/` separating CPU from GPU evidence.

checks.note: Derive both strategies on paper before opening the printed solution.

rubric.pass: Outputs plus input and weight gradients match the oracle, and collective records name each communicating move.
rubric.strong: A second sharding or activation choice replays cleanly, and one seeded defect shows which check catches it.

rubric.pass: Sharded loss, tied weights, norms and residuals match oracles, with gain sums and accounting kept.
rubric.strong: Reset-position and repeated-mask mutations fail named assertions, and padding policy is exercised.

rubric.pass: Ring outputs and gradients match dense attention, uneven and empty cases pass, and illegal layouts are rejected.
rubric.strong: Ownership mutations fail specific assertions, and the redundant rotation removal keeps the match.

rubric.pass: The ledger covers parameters, activations and collectives, separating payload, traffic, saved and peak memory.
rubric.strong: Synchronous and asynchronous paths match oracles, candidates name their limiting constraint, and GPU traces report exposed communication honestly.

miniProject.feedsInto: The `parallel/` mechanisms, oracles, ledgers and candidate tables feed pipeline and expert composition, the multidimensional plan and the capstone.
